blindSummary:
This state/province recorded 5 killings of trans people (trans women and people of a local trans-feminine identity category) in 2025, matching the 5-killings band shared with two other states, and 5 in 2024 as well. Against a population of ~8.7 million the 2025 rate is about 0.57 per million per year, above the national figure of ~0.38. The state/province spans a vast river-basin interior, where the dossier's finding that roughly two-thirds of killings happen outside the capitals means interior municipal exposure is hard to assess and protection infrastructure is thinner for a visitor travelling beyond the capital.

No local legal or ordinance finding was identified; the signal is the sustained above-national killing counts and the river-basin geography. For comparison, the two top-count states recorded 8 killings each in 2025, one of them on a population of ~9 million.
blindSourceSummaries: The national trans-murder monitoring association's ninth annual dossier (released 26 Jan 2026, reported by a broadcast outlet): the country recorded 80 murders of trans people in 2025, 34% down on 2024 but with at least 75 attempted homicides and crimes marked by excessive violence; 2025 per-state counts in descending order - 8, 8, 7, 7, 5, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2; 1,261 murders over 2017-2025 (avg 140/year); 97% of victims were trans women (including a local trans-feminine identity category), over half aged 18-29, 70% black among racially-identified cases; 67.5% of killings happened in interior cities rather than capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policies are harder; the country has led the global ranking since 2008. Places this state/province in the 5-killings band for 2025.

Coverage of the association's 2024 dossier (27 Jan 2025): 122 trans people (trans women and the local trans-feminine identity category) were murdered in the country in 2024, 16% below 2023's 145 and just under the 2008-2024 average of 125; five victims were human-rights defenders, including a city-council alternate; 95.9% of victims were trans women (including that category); the highest 2024 state counts were 16, 12 and 11, with three states recording none; at least 68% (83 cases) occurred in interior cities outside state capitals; 1,179 killings confirmed 2017-2024; official statistics are unreliable due to misclassification and underreporting. Provides the 2024 national figures and interior-concentration pattern behind this state/province's context.
